Input Formats¶

cuDART reads simulation data in the form of .npy files which MUST have dtype=np.float32. The formatting of these files depends on the intended operation mode. Each .npy file should have the shape

  • (nx,ny,nz): if running without relativisitc boosting

  • (nx,ny,nz,4): if running with relativistic boosting

where here nx, ny and nz are the number of cells in each cardinal direction and in the relativistic case the fourth index spans emissivity and velocity in each of the cardinal directions.

It is worth noting that Python genarlly does not ensure its arrays have consistent C-style ordering. It is up to the user to ensure that the saved .npy data has true C-style array ordering and has not been reordered through stride meta-data alteration. C-style ordering can be forced in Python using data = np.array(data, order="C").

Input data may be unlabelled, or labeled:

  • Unlabelled mode: each simulation snapshot is stored a single .npy file

  • Labelled mode: each simulation snapshot is stored within a directory, containing multiple .npy files for each sub-domian, and a header file header.txt which contains additional information

Unlabelled Mode¶

Unlabelled mode is designed for rendering simulation domains that have a single homogenous resolution. In this case, the input can be a single .npy file; the code will automatically assume that the simulation cells are cubic and that the longest domain side has a length of unity. If the domain does not feature cubic cells, or contains multiple sub-domains in different resolutions, then labelled mode should be used. The data directory containing unlabelled simulation data might take the form

data_directory
├── snapshot00000.npy
├── snapshot00001.npy
├── snapshot00002.npy
├── …

Labelled Mode¶

Labelled mode is designed to render simulation domains composed of multiple sub-domains which may not have the same resolution. In this case, the data directory should contain a .npy file for each subdomian, and an additional header file to label the spatial position/extents of each sub-domain (as well as meta-data concerning the number of cells in each domain). The directory containing labelled simulation data might take the form

data_directory
├── snapshot00000
│ ├── header.txt
│ ├── meshblock00000.npy
│ ├── meshblock00001.npy
│ ├── …
├── snapshot00001
│ ├── header.txt
│ ├── meshblock00000.npy
│ ├── meshblock00001.npy
│ ├── …
├── …

Header files can be automatically formatted using the Mesh class (see Example Usage <example>).

Converting Simulation Data¶

While useful for manipulation in Python, .npy files are not the standard outputs from hydrodynamic simulations codes. To support conversion between standard simulation file formats and the .npy files required by cuDART, additional functions are included in pysrc. Currently conversion support is available for the .vtk files output from PLUTO, and the .hdf5 files output from Athena++.
